property_summary: After initialization, MinSum cannot be changed; the bug allows it to be changed after initialization.
Once initialized, MinSum cannot be changed by any subsequent call to SetMinSum; the buggy function without nonReentrant_ allows a re-entrant call to modify MinSum after initialization.
After initialization, a reentrant call from a recipient during Collect cannot change MinSum; the buggy version allows a reentrant SetMinSum to change MinSum mid-Collect.

After initialization and any call to SetMinSum, reading MinSum always returns the value that was set by the call; in the buggy version, a re-entrant call triggered during SetMinSum can overwrite MinSum after the initial call completes, so the final MinSum differs from the value originally passed.
After initialization, any top-level call to SetMinSum should revert; the buggy version without nonReentrant_ allows a successful call after initialization, changing MinSum.

After initialization, MinSum can only be set once and never changed; the buggy version without nonReentrant_ allows a reentrant call during Put to re-enter SetMinSum and change MinSum after initialization, making a subsequent Collect succeed with a lower MinSum than intended.
After any sequence of calls, MinSum can only be set once when uninitialized; the buggy modifier allows MinSum to be overwritten after initialization.
After initialization, calling SetMinSum must revert; the buggy nonReentrant_ always allows entry, letting MinSum be overwritten post-initialization.
After Initialized, SetMinSum must revert (reference); the buggy modifier allows it to succeed and change MinSum.
After the contract is initialized, MinSum must never change; the buggy modifier allows SetMinSum to succeed and overwrite MinSum after initialization.
After initialization, any call to SetMinSum must revert and leave MinSum unchanged; the buggy modifier always allows entry, enabling overwriting of MinSum after initialization.
For any call to SetMinSum, MinSum must remain unchanged if the contract is already initialized; the mutant allows a reentrant call during initialization to set MinSum to a different value.

For any two calls to SetMinSum (with arbitrary values) made while the contract is NOT yet initialized, the final MinSum must equal the value supplied in the second call; the buggy mutant (missing require(!locked_)) allows a reentrant call during the first call to overwrite MinSum with a stale value.

After any sequence of calls to SetMinSum that leaves the contract initialized, the final MinSum must equal the value supplied in the last successful call; the buggy mutant allows a reentrant call during initialization to overwrite MinSum with a value different from the last successful call.

For any call to SetMinSum, if the contract is not yet initialized and the call is not reentered during itself, MinSum equals the argument; the bug allows a reentrant call that overwrites MinSum during the same external call, violating this.

After any single external call to SetMinSum with the contract uninitialized, MinSum must equal the supplied value; the bug allows a reentrant callback during SetMinSum to overwrite MinSum with a different value, violating this.
After one invocation, MinSum equals the passed value; after two invocations, the second call changes MinSum in the buggy version but must revert in the reference.

In the reference contract, any call to SetMinSum after initialization always reverts, so MinSum can only be set once. In the buggy contract, the nonReentrant_ modifier fails to lock, allowing SetMinSum to be called multiple times and thus MinSum can be changed after initialization.
After initialization, any call to SetMinSum must revert, leaving MinSum unchanged; the bug allows a second call to succeed and alter MinSum.
After initialization, SetMinSum must revert on any subsequent call, but the bug allows it to succeed, changing MinSum.

The nonReentrant_ modifier must prevent re-entrant calls to SetMinSum, ensuring that after a call to SetMinSum, MinSum reflects only the latest call; the bug removes the lock, allowing a re-entrant call to overwrite MinSum so that after the outer call completes, MinSum does not equal the last value passed to SetMinSum.

For any initial MinSum x and any re-entrant call that sets MinSum to y during SetMinSum execution, after SetMinSum(y) completes, MinSum must equal y; the buggy non-locking modifier allows a re-entrant SetMinSum(x) to override it, leaving MinSum == x after the outer call completes.

After any non-reverting call to SetMinSum, the public state variable MinSum must equal the argument supplied to that latest call; the buggy non-locking modifier allows a re-entrant call to overwrite MinSum during the original call, so the final MinSum may differ from the original argument.

After any external call to SetMinSum that does not revert, the value of the public state variable MinSum must equal the argument supplied to that latest call, but the buggy non-locking modifier allows a re-entrant caller to overwrite MinSum during the same transaction, so MinSum may not reflect the final argument.

For any allowed call to SetMinSum where the caller is not a contract, MinSum after the call is exactly the argument of that call; the buggy modifier allows a re-entrant contract to change MinSum within the call, so the final value may differ.
After initialization, SetLogFile cannot change Log to a new address in the reference, but the buggy version allows repeated calls to change Log.
